name: Ashbel
overview: Ashbel was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, uniquely identified as a son of Benjamin. He is noted among the descendants of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking his place in the early history of the Israelite people. His lineage is associated with the Ashbelites, a clan named after him, emphasizing his role in the tribal structure of Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Ashbel likely means 'man of Baal' or 'having a long upper lip,' reflecting common ancient Hebrew naming conventions. Another related name, Jediael, means 'known of God [El],' though it is not directly attributed to Ashbel himself. These names highlight the cultural and religious contexts of the time without direct divine naming.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ashbel as a son of Benjamin, establishing his direct paternal lineage. An inferred relationship suggests Bilhan as his father, though this is not explicitly stated for Ashbel himself but linked to his broader family line. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are documented in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Ashbel's significance lies in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who moved to Egypt, a pivotal event in the biblical narrative leading to the formation of the Israelite nation. The mention of the Ashbelites in later genealogical records underscores his lasting impact on the tribal organization of Benjamin. His presence in these lists connects him to God's providential plan in preserving and expanding the covenant people.
